description: A trigger sequencer with eight tracks and four pages of eight steps, made to be played from a MIDI grid controller

params.text: Turns that step of its track on or off; while LENGTH, EUCLIDEAN or ROTATE is armed the press sets that instead
Turns that track on or off; a track that is off sends nothing to either of its outputs
Shows that quarter of the sequence on the grid, without interrupting any track
Sets every track back to its first step
Advances every track by one step
Arms the grid so that the next step pressed becomes the last step of that track, which is what lets tracks run at different lengths
Arms MIDI learn, so that a control moved on the MIDI controller and a control then clicked here are mapped to one another
At one the main output of that track follows the programmed steps exactly; below one it is the chance that a programmed step plays, and above one it adds a chance that an unprogrammed step plays
Sets the chance that a step of that track which is not programmed plays on the alt output
Arms the grid so that the next step pressed sets the number of hits spread evenly across that track's length
Arms the grid so that pressing the first step of a track rotates its pattern one step left, and pressing the second step rotates it one step right

inputs.text: A rising edge sets every track back to its first step
A rising edge advances every track by one step, and the voltage present here is what the outputs pass on, so the output pulses keep the width of the clock

outputs.text: Passes the clock pulse through whenever the programmed step on that track plays
Passes the clock pulse through on steps of that track which are not programmed, for ghost hits and alternating voices

notes: a grid controller lights up only once a device is chosen in both MIDI IN and MIDI OUT; each of those displays carries its own menus for the driver, the device and the channel
one grid controller is used, and the eight steps of a page map to one row of its grid
factory MIDI mappings ship as module presets, listed under Factory presets in the Preset submenu of the panel menu
the factory mappings cover the APC Mini, the Akai APC Key 25, the Launchpad Mk1 Mini, the Launchpad Pro Mk1, the Launchpad Mk2 and the Launchpad Mk3 Mini
the Launchpad Mk3 mapping needs Factory Custom Mode 3 active on the controller, which is slot 3, the User button, by default
the strip marked SEQUENCE draws all thirty two steps of all eight tracks at once, with the step now playing marked on each track
menu: Use Rotary Encoders — reads the probability controls as endless encoders rather than as absolute faders
Clear all Midi Mappings — removes every mapping made by MIDI learn
Clear Midi Mapping — arms a mode in which the next control clicked here, or the next control moved on the controller, has its mapping removed
Midi Learn Parameter First — reverses the order of MIDI learn, so a control here is clicked before the controller is moved
Slow midi feedback — thins out the messages sent back to the controller
None — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for a step that is off, 0 to 127, which is what picks that pad's colour
Step — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for a programmed step, 0 to 127
Index — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for the step now playing, 0 to 127
Loop — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for the last step of a track, 0 to 127
Step & Loop — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for a step that is both programmed and the last step of its track, 0 to 127
Probability Notch Width — adds a flat zone in the middle of the main probability controls, so an imprecise fader gives exactly the programmed pattern; None 0%, Slim 20%, Mid 35% or Wide 50%
